0.content: Albedo's Campsite (also: Albedo's camp, Albedo's outpost): Albedo's Campsite is a small laboratory outpost inside a cave in Dragonspine, used by the alchemist Albedo. It lies on the path from the Entombed City's Ancient Palace to its Outskirts.

1.content: Anemo Archon Statue (also: Statue of Barbatos, Barbatos Statue, Statue of the Anemo Archon): The Anemo Archon Statue is the large stone likeness of Barbatos, the Anemo Archon, standing in the plaza in front of Favonius Cathedral in Mondstadt City. It shows a hooded figure with two wings and hands cupped together.

2.content:
Angel's Share (also: Angels Share): Angel's Share is a tavern in Mondstadt City, established and funded by the long-standing Dawn Winery. Charles is its bartender, and the winery's owner Diluc sometimes takes a shift himself. It is the traditional home of Mondstadt's wine trade and has a friendly rival in the Cat's Tail.

People: Charles, the bartender, has worked here more than a decade as a Dawn Winery employee.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tavern is open and operating; nothing in later content changes it.

3.content:
Apathic Interval (also: Interval of No Thought): The Apathic Interval is the first stage of being "uplifted" into the Temple of Space, the floating hall above Windrest Peak. Individuals chosen from vanished eras are cast here and must reach a state of complete emptiness, giving up every desire through Maranasati meditation, before they may enter the temple proper. Depending on the person this can take a few years or several centuries. The change is deep: it alters personality and leaves a person unable to obtain a Vision.

Status as of 7.1: As of 6.5 (and unchanged through 7.1) the Interval is still guarded by Caskets but no new people are being uplifted.

4.content:
Arcadia (also: Great Arcadia): Arcadia, also called Great Arcadia, was a civilization in Mondstadt's vast oak forests, between what are now Windrest Peak, Windrise and Windwail Highland. A part of Teyvat's unified civilization, it was a holy city of plenty, favoured by heaven, that worshipped Istaroth and Asmoday and later the Three Moons. It was entombed in endless winter when the War of Funerary Flame came.

Status as of 7.1: Long lost as a civilization; ruins and records only as of 7.1.

5.content:
Brightcrown Canyon: Brightcrown Canyon is a rocky canyon in the Brightcrown Mountains, on Mondstadt's north-western side. At its north-eastern end lies the eastern entrance to Stormterror's Lair, the ruined capital of the old storm god Decarabian. Hilichurls roam its ancient mechanical guards and ruins.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing new is recorded; still ruined and dangerous.

6.content:
Brightcrown Mountains: The Brightcrown Mountains are the rugged northwestern part of Mondstadt. They hold Brightcrown Canyon and, at the heart of the range, the ruins of Old Mondstadt, the walled city of Decarabian, God of Storms. During the Prologue the ruins were Stormterror's Lair, the sleeping place of the dragon Dvalin.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ruins are quiet. The storm barrier from the Prologue is gone.

7.content:
Cage of Suchness (also: Atrium of Suchness): The Cage of Suchness is the highest point of the Temple of Space, the floating hall above Windrest Peak in Mondstadt. It was the home of the god Asmoday and her two Watchers, Nihilita and Melanta, and from here they oversaw the temple. It lies beyond the Corridor of Nothingness and can be reached only by laying down all of one's memories. After Asmoday's disappearance it became the seat of the Watcher Melanta, who ruled the temple's inhabitants harshly until the Traveler defeated him there.

Status as of 7.1: As of 6.5 and still at 7.1, Melanta is gone and the Cage is empty.

8.content:
Cape Oath: Cape Oath is a headland at the south-eastern corner of Mondstadt's surroundings, bordering Galesong Hill. A local legend says two lovers swore an oath to each other here, and young couples still come for the sunrise and sunset. A time tunnel on the cape leads to Musk Reef, the island that holds the entrance to the Spiral Abyss.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 unchanged.

9.content:
Cecilia Garden (also: Cecilia Garden domain): Cecilia Garden is a Forgery domain near Wolvendom in Windwail Highland, Mondstadt. The entrance text says Cecilia flowers, which grow only on high cliffs, once bloomed here in greenhouses, and that the ancient civilisation that enjoyed their scent was lost along with the sea of white flowers. It is an ancient sacrificial altar flooded with Hydro energy, and clearing it yields weapon ascension materials.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the domain is open and unchanged since 1.0; nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content alters it.

10.content:
Cider Lake: Cider Lake is the large freshwater lake in Starfell Valley that holds the island on which Mondstadt City stands. Its water is crystal clear, cool and never freezes, and its headwaters are credited with Mondstadt's famous ciders and wines. It has become a symbol of the nation.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 unchanged.

11.content:
Dadaupa Gorge: Dadaupa Gorge is a rugged area of Galesong Hill in Mondstadt, home to three hilichurl tribes: the Meaty, the Sleeper and the Eclipse. At its centre lies the Forgotten Sword Cemetery, which witnessed the ancient battle against the monsters of Khaenri'ah.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 hilichurls still hold the gorge and the cemetery remains studied.

12.content:
Dawn Winery (also: Dawn Winery estate, Manor of Daybreak): The Dawn Winery is the chief winery of Mondstadt, on a hill in Windwail Highland southwest of the capital. It specialises in dandelion wine and is the estate of the Ragnvindr family, which has owned it for about a thousand years. Its owner is Diluc Ragnvindr, who inherited it four years before the Prologue when his father Crepus died. A game viewpoint describes it as a pilgrimage site for anyone who loves the bottle.

Status as of 7.1: In operation as of 7.1, owned by Diluc.

13.content:
Dawn Winery Manor (also: Manor of Daybreak, Diluc Manor): The Dawn Winery Manor is the central house of the Dawn Winery in Mondstadt's Windwail Highland, the Ragnvindr family estate that Diluc now owns. Its housemaids and butler run the winery's day-to-day affairs. Its name is unofficial: the manga calls it Diluc Manor, and the game's own text calls it the Manor of Daybreak.

People: Staff here: the head housemaid Adelinde, the butler Elzer, and the maids Hillie and Moco.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the manor remains the winery's home and offices; no change in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content is recorded on the wiki.

14.content:
Decarabian's Mondstadt (also: Old Mondstadt, Decarabian's City): Decarabian's Mondstadt, usually called Old Mondstadt, was the original home of Mondstadt's people: a walled capital built in a deep valley by the God of Storms, Decarabian, who ruled from a great tower. His people rebelled and killed him about 2,600 years ago, after which the new Anemo Archon Barbatos led them to Cider Lake. The valley is now the ruin-filled area called Stormterror's Lair.

Status as of 7.1: Abandoned ruins as of 7.1.

15.content:
Decarabian's Tower (also: Tower of Decarabian): Decarabian's Tower is the great ruined tower at the middle of Old Mondstadt, from which the God of Storms Decarabian ruled and watched over his people. His death blew away part of it. Centuries later the wounded dragon Dvalin laired in the ruin, and the Traveler climbs it in the Prologue.

Status as of 7.1: A ruin, open to climb as of 7.1.

key: Pavilion of Scorching Sands and Blazing Sun
16.content:
Desert Pavilion (also: Pavilion of Scorching Sands and Blazing Sun, Desert Pavilion: Mirage): The Desert Pavilion is the Temple of Space's exhibition area for sculpture and architecture, built in the style of the desert temples of Sumeru. Its loading-screen text says that though every grand tower in the world will crumble into sand, towers built upon sand remain here forever. It was reconstructed from memory by the temple's Uplifted residents. Under the Watcher Melanta's rule its people were punished by being turned into sand statues, until the Traveler freed them in 6.5.

Status as of 7.1: As of 6.5 (unchanged through 7.1) the sand curse is lifted and the residents are restored.

17.content:
Devil's Cut (also: Devils Cut, The Devil's Cut): Devil's Cut is the tavern of Dornman Port, in Windrest Peak (opened in 6.5). Its owner is Groovy. The name pairs with Mondstadt City's Angel's Share, and the two taverns are counterparts. The port tavern serves sailors, merchants and locals.

People: Groovy is the tavern owner. Odolf, a Dornman Port businessman, drinks here.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tavern is open and unchanged; nothing in 6.x-7.1 content after its debut alters it.

key: The Harbor Where a Thousand Winds Converge
18.content:
Dornman Port (also: The Harbor Where a Thousand Winds Converge): Dornman Port is the busy port town of northern Mondstadt, on Windrest Peak north of Cider Lake. Its loading screen calls it a bustling harbor and one of the continent's major trade hubs, welcoming merchant ships from many nations. In the aristocratic era it was the fief of the Gunnhildr Clan. Mondstadt knights are stationed here, and the port has no church.

Status as of 7.1: A thriving trade port with a Knights of Favonius base as of 7.1.

19.content:
Dragonspine (also: Vindagnyr): Dragonspine is a huge snow-covered mountain in Mondstadt, one of the most dangerous places in the nation: its snow never melts and its cold kills the unprepared. It was once called Vindagnyr, a green mountain where the ancient kingdom of Sal Vindagnyr flourished until a Celestial Nail, the Skyfrost Nail, fell on it and buried it in endless winter. About five hundred years ago the Abyssal dragon Durin fell dead here after his battle with Dvalin, giving the mountain its present name. The alchemist Albedo keeps a research camp on its slopes.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Dragonspine is still frozen and hazardous. Durin's heart has been inert since Albedo drained it during Paralogism, and Durin's name now belongs to the gentle young man created in his place. After the 7.1 Archon Quest the Skyfrost Nail began showing a strange change, and Albedo is watching it from the summit.

20.content: Dragonspine Adventurer Camp: A small adventurers' camp on the outskirts of Dragonspine, on the path from Dadaupa Gorge up toward the snowbound mountain. The chef Harris built it so adventurers would have somewhere to rest and a hot bowl of soup after a hard day in the cold.

21.content: Drunkard Gorge: Drunkard Gorge is a stretch of road in Windwail Highland that separates Dawn Winery from Wolvendom. It used to be a popular place for travelling merchants, but it now has a reputation for danger and most people have left.

22.content: Durin's Core (also: Durin's heart, heart of Durin): Durin's Core is the still-beating heart of Durin, the Abyssal dragon killed above Dragonspine, found in Wyrmrest Valley. Its ominous vitality could turn Strange Teeth into Empowered Dragonteeth, and it gives off warmth.

23.content:
Entombed City - Ancient Palace (also: Entombed City Ancient Palace): The Entombed City - Ancient Palace is the frozen palace district of Sal Vindagnyr, an ancient kingdom on the mountain now called Dragonspine. The official description calls it an ancient city that lies silent beneath the eternal ice. Cryo hilichurls prowl its ruins.

Status as of 7.1: Still buried in ice as of 7.1; no later change is recorded.

24.content:
Entombed City - Outskirts (also: Entombed City Outskirts): The Entombed City - Outskirts is the outer edge of Sal Vindagnyr's buried city on Dragonspine. The official description says the city has been entombed by snow so deeply that it is nearly indistinguishable from its former self. Cryo hilichurls and the Cryo Hypostasis make it dangerous.

Status as of 7.1: Frozen ruins, unchanged as of 7.1.

25.content: Entrance to Stormterror's Lair: The Entrance to Stormterror's Lair is a set of ruins in Decarabian's architectural style in Brightcrown Canyon. It once led straight into the capital of Decarabian, the old God of Storms, and is now the way into the area known as Stormterror's Lair.

26.content:
Falcon Coast: Falcon Coast is a long sandy coast in Galesong Hill, east of Mondstadt, stretching from Windrise to the sea. With Cape Oath, it shelters a bay on three sides. Citizens stroll its white sand and shallow water, and falcons can be seen above the waves.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 unchanged.

27.content:
Favonius Cathedral (also: Mondstadt Cathedral, Cathedral of Favonius): The Favonius Cathedral is the great Gothic-looking church at the top of Mondstadt City, standing behind the plaza with the giant statue of the Anemo Archon Barbatos. The Church of Favonius runs it as the centre of Barbatos worship: nuns pray and hear confessions there, Deaconess Barbara works there, and its guarded basement held the Holy Lyre der Himmel, which the Traveler tried to steal for Venti in the Prologue.

People: Clergy of the Church of Favonius: Deaconess Barbara (healer, singer and "idol" of Mondstadt), the nun Rosaria (who skips nearly every Church duty), Deacon Dahlia, and, since his return from Nod-Krai, Seneschal Seamus Pegg.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Cathedral is in normal use. Seamus Pegg has returned from Varka's expedition and works there again, taking on work the clergy carried alone for years. The Church has the Holy Lyre back, and Barbara has refused to lend it out again.

28.content: Field Tiller (also: Weird Statue, First Field Tiller, Tyrant's Final Fury): The Field Tiller is an inactive Ruin Guard on the upper deck of the central tower of Stormterror's Lair in the Brightcrown Mountains. Before the quest We Will Be Reunited the game calls it a Weird Statue. It is the original prototype of the war machines now known as Ruin Guards.

29.content:
Floral Whisper: Floral Whisper is a small flower shop in the market district of Mondstadt City. Its owner is Flora, who sells flowers for Mora. The shop is open from 06:00 to 19:00.

Status as of 7.1: Operating as of 7.1, as far as sources show.

30.content: Forgotten Sword Cemetery (also: Sword Cemetery, Unnamed Sword Cemetery): The Forgotten Sword Cemetery lies in the middle of the large lake in Dadaupa Gorge, Galesong Hill. It is described as having witnessed the battle against the monsters of Khaenri'ah, and it is guarded by a three-layer seal.

31.content:
Fragrant Whispers: Fragrant Whispers is a flower shop in the middle of Dornman Port, the port town in the northern Windrest Peak area of Mondstadt. Alodia owns it. It first appeared in Version 6.5.

Status as of 7.1: Operating as of 7.1, as far as sources show.

32.content: Frostbearing Tree (also: Frostbearing Trees): The Frostbearing Tree is a new sprout of an ancient Irminsul tree that the Skyfrost Nail destroyed. It was revived by the blood of the Abyssal dragon Durin and grows in Dragonspine, marked with red rather than the usual blue.

33.content:
Galesong Hill: Galesong Hill is the windswept eastern part of Mondstadt, a region of open hills running down to the sea. Its best-known spot is Windrise, a plain under a giant oak where a Statue of the Seven stands, said to mark the place where Vennessa ascended to Celestia. East of it lie the Falcon Coast and Cape Oath, favourite places for walks and for young couples, while the rugged Dadaupa Gorge belongs to hilichurl tribes.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Galesong Hill is peaceful countryside; none of the pages read for this entry records a change to it after Version 1.0.

34.content:
Golden Apple Archipelago (also: Haar Islands, Golden Archipelago): The Golden Apple Archipelago is a set of mountainous islands in the sea east of Mondstadt. It was a limited-time summer event map: first as the setting of Midsummer Island Adventure (1.6), when Klee and her friends followed a mysterious letter from "Dodo-King" to it, and again in Summertime Odyssey (2.8) with a new look. It was formerly the fog-bound Haar Islands. It is not accessible as of 7.1.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the archipelago is not accessible: both event runs have ended and the map is removed. Nothing in Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) content revisits it. Its events remain canon but are not widely known.

35.content:
Good Hunter: Good Hunter is the most popular restaurant in Mondstadt City. The waitress Sara serves simple food and cooking ingredients and sells recipes. It stands in the market district, across from Mondstadt General Goods.

Status as of 7.1: Open and busy as of 7.1, as far as sources show.

36.content:
Goth Grand Hotel (also: Goth Hotel): The Goth Grand Hotel is Mondstadt City's hotel, owned by Ludwig Goth. The Fatui delegation has reserved the entire building, and the guard Luke stands at the door to keep unauthorised people out. Ordinary guests can no longer stay.

People: Owner: Ludwig Goth. Door guard: the Fatui member Luke.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the wiki records no end to the Fatui reservation; treat the hotel as still closed to the public unless a scene says otherwise.

37.content: Hexenzirkel's Island in the Sky (also: Hexenzirkel's floating island, Hexenzirkel tea party island): Hexenzirkel's Island in the Sky is a floating island above Falcon Coast where the Hexenzirkel used to hold tea parties. Barbatos looks after access to it, and one has to speak an incantation at the cliff to enter.

38.content:
Imaginarium Theater (also: Theater Lobby, Mysterious Room): The Imaginarium Theater is a hidden room entered from Mondstadt's Knights of Favonius library, a stage and lounge where guests perform fantasy plays. It is looked after by Wolfy, a small talking stuffed wolf. It appeared in Version 4.7.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1, with new seasons rotating in.

39.content:
Knights of Favonius Base (also: Dornman Port Knights base, Windrest Peak Knights base): The Knights of Favonius Base is the Knights' forward base at Dornman Port in Windrest Peak, built around the 5th (Ranged) Company. Detachments from the 6th (Logistics), 7th (Combined Arms), 8th (Support) and 10th (Investigation) Companies are stationed there too. "Knights of Favonius Base" is an unofficial name.

People: Vice Captain Lohen commands the Ranged Company's people here, among them the snipers Gunther and Ursula.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the base is active and the Ranged Company remains stationed there.

40.content:
Knights of Favonius Headquarters (also: Knights Headquarters, Favonius Headquarters, Mondstadt Library, Knights of Favonius Library): The Knights of Favonius Headquarters is the order's main building in Mondstadt City and the centre of the nation's government. Inside are the Grand Master's office, where Acting Grand Master Jean works almost without pause, Chief Alchemist Albedo's office on the second floor, a locked solitary confinement room that Klee has more or less made her own, and the Mondstadt Library, kept by the librarian Lisa. The library is the largest in northern Teyvat and is open to everyone.

People: Jean (Acting Grand Master), Lisa (librarian), Albedo (Chief Alchemist), Klee (when confined), and the knights and captains who report here, including Kaeya.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the headquarters is fully active. Varka has been home since 6.4, Jean still holds the title Acting Grand Master and works long hours here, and Lisa still runs the library.

41.content:
Knights of Favonius Ruins: The Knights of Favonius Ruins are the remains of an ancient battlefield beneath Dornman Port, where the Knights of Favonius fought the Abyss and where their dead lie buried. They are reached from the base of the port's old lighthouse. The ruins first appear in version 6.5.

Status as of 7.1: The alarm is quiet, the graves are tended and the ruins are open as of 7.1.

42.content:
Luyang Academy (also: Amidst the Ink-Tinged Mist): Luyang Academy is the part of the Temple of Space devoted to painting, built in the style of Liyue architecture. Though it is a gallery of paintings from many eras, the sages who first named it believed that books and paintings are one and the same, hence "academy". Under the Watcher Melanta's rule its artists were punished by being turned into ink blots or sealed in paintings. In 6.5 the Traveler, Paimon, Zeitlind and Dex freed them by restoring paintings into real space.

Status as of 7.1: As of 6.5 (and still at 7.1) the Academy is freed and its painters live there again.

43.content:
Mahavaipulya Chamber (also: Mahavaipulya Hall, Mahavaipulya Archives, The Moving Finger Writes): The Mahavaipulya Chamber is the Temple of Space's library, devoted to ancient texts and to the new novels written by some of its Uplifted residents. Its loading-screen text says it stores books from various eras. Because the residents' stories blurred history and fiction, the Watcher Melanta pressed them between the pages; in 6.5 the Traveler, Paimon, Zeitlind and Dex restored the library and freed them.

Status as of 7.1: As of 6.5 (unchanged through 7.1) the library is restored and its residents free.

44.content:
Midsummer Courtyard (also: Sommernachtgarten, Midsummer Courtyard domain): Midsummer Courtyard is a Domain of Blessing near Starsnatch Cliff in Starfell Valley, Mondstadt. Per its entrance text, when the ancient lost civilisation fell, the once magnificent Sommernachtgarten ("Summer Night Garden") was buried underground, leaving only ancient trees and stones to recall its glory. It is an ancient blessed altar full of monsters that fear Pyro, and clearing it rewards artifacts.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the domain is open and unchanged since 1.0.

45.content:
Millhaven (also: Blossoms in Fragrant Bloom): Millhaven is a peaceful, tranquil village in Windrest Peak, in northern Mondstadt, known for its sweet-smelling flowers and fragrance products. It is an idyllic place of windmills and fields of the Windrest Flower. Its loading screen calls it a peaceful and tranquil town.

Status as of 7.1: Peaceful and unchanged as of 7.1; no Millhaven content from 7.0-7.1 was found.

46.content:
Mona's Laboratory: Mona's Laboratory is a house at the southern end of Mondstadt City, a little past Schulz's Blacksmith. Goth owns it and Mona, the astrologist, rents it. For most of the game its door is shut.

Status as of 7.1: Nothing after the quests is recorded; the door stays closed to the player outside them.

47.content:
Mondstadt (also: Mond, City of Freedom): Mondstadt is the nation of freedom in northeastern Teyvat, the land of the Anemo Archon Barbatos, who walks among his people unrecognised as the bard Venti and deliberately does not rule. The Knights of Favonius govern in practice; the Church of Favonius tends worship. The capital, Mondstadt City, sits on an island in Cider Lake amid windmills and rolling green country. Mondstadters are easygoing lovers of taverns, song and festivals, proud of the gifts they credit to their god: dandelions, flight (gliding) and wine.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Mondstadt is at peace. Grand Master Varka has returned from the long expedition to Nod-Krai but still travels to the Knights' outpost there, so Jean remains Acting Grand Master. Venti no longer holds his Gnosis.

48.content:
Mondstadt City (also: City of Mondstadt, Crown of the North, City of Wind, City of Bards, City of Pastorals): Mondstadt City, the "City of Wind" and capital of Mondstadt, stands on a large island in Cider Lake in western Starfell Valley, ringed by a stone wall and reached by a long bridge. Cobbled streets climb past windmills and half-timbered houses to a plaza where a giant statue of the Anemo Archon Barbatos stands before the Favonius Cathedral. The Knights of Favonius govern from their headquarters here; the city is known for its relaxed pace, bards, festivals and taverns.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the city is at peace. Jean still works as Acting Grand Master from the headquarters, Grand Master Varka is home from the Nod-Krai expedition, and Durin now lives in Mondstadt. The Archon Quest has moved to Snezhnaya, and no new crisis in the city is shown.

49.content:
Mondstadt General Goods: Mondstadt General Goods is a small shop in the market district of Mondstadt City, run by Blanche. It sells cooking ingredients and is open at all hours. An order board stands beside it.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1, as far as sources show.

50.content:
Mondstadt Market District: The Mondstadt Market District is the shopping quarter at the lower end of Mondstadt City. Its two-storey buildings have tan walls and red-tiled roofs and house shops, a tavern and the stalls of merchants and craftsmen.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 unchanged.

51.content:
Mural Room: The Mural Room is a hidden chamber on Dragonspine that holds frescoes painted by the Princess of Sal Vindagnyr. A claymore, the Snow-Tombed Starsilver, stands stuck in a platform at its centre. It preserves the kingdom's image from before the snow and the outlander Imunlaukr's farewell.

Status as of 7.1: Unchanged as of 7.1; open to anyone who completes the objective.

52.content:
Musk Reef (also: Pilos Peak): Musk Reef is a small island off the coast of Galesong Hill in Mondstadt. Its main feature is the portal to the Spiral Abyss, and it is reached through a bluish-purple time tunnel at Cape Oath (or by gliding there from the cape). Long ago, before Barbatos reshaped the land, it was the summit of a great mountain called Pilos Peak.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Musk Reef remains an ordinary accessible island in Mondstadt, still holding the Spiral Abyss portal. The meteorite crisis of 1.1 ended long ago. Nothing in Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) content changes it.

53.content: Nameless Island (also: the nameless island, Mondstadt sundial island): The Nameless Island is a small, uninhabited island off the coast northeast of Starfell Valley in Mondstadt, with no name on the map. A weathered sundial stands at its centre, and the island is where the world quest Time and Wind begins.

54.content:
Old Sanatorium Site: The Old Sanatorium Site is a former mountain sanatorium on Windrest Peak, torn down a few years ago. It stands above the ruins of a temple left behind when the Temple of Space was lifted into the heavens, and its Anemo Archon statue is the gateway up to that temple. Locals say that whoever visits the sanatorium stays in the enchanted hills forever.

Status as of 7.1: Demolished and decaying as of 7.1; an access point to the Temple of Space.

key: Pillar Hall of Space: Front Hall
Pillar Hall of Space: Rear Hall
55.content:
Path of the Forgotten World (also: Pillar Hall of Space: Front Hall, Pillar Hall of Space: Rear Hall): The Path of the Forgotten World is the entrance area of the Temple of Space, the floating hall above Windrest Peak in Mondstadt. The wiki calls it the entrance area, leading toward the central Pillar Hall. Creatures from lost ages are exhibited along it. The area has very little recorded lore of its own.

Status as of 7.1: As of 6.5 (unchanged through 7.1) the Path is open and uneventful.

56.content:
Peak of Vindagnyr (also: Elegiac Rime): The Peak of Vindagnyr is a Domain of Blessing on the summit of Dragonspine, at the Skyfrost Nail. It was once a ritual site close to the sky where Sal Vindagnyr's priests ascended to face the heavens, until a frigid nail from the firmament buried it in the mountainside. The cold inside is a trial in itself: visitors must conquer it to pass.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it remains a permanent Domain of Blessing, unchanged since 4.8.

57.content:
Pillar Hall Central Zone (also: Hall of a Thousand Pillars, Pillar Hall of Space, Center of the Pillar Hall): The Pillar Hall Central Zone is the centre of the Temple of Space, the floating hall above Windrest Peak. It houses the Memory Core, a storage device holding information about unknown civilisations. The hall is lined with display boards presenting relics of many eras, and it is the safest place in the temple: suppression-type guards cannot enter it. The philosopher Istoria and the shopkeeper Josephus keep to it, and it is the hub from which the three themed exhibition areas are reached.

Status as of 7.1: As of 6.5 (unchanged through 7.1) the hall is a safe hub for the freed residents and for visitors.

58.content:
Sal Vindagnyr (also: Vindagnyr, Entombed City, Kingdom of Sal Vindagnyr): Sal Vindagnyr was an ancient kingdom on the mountain once called Vindagnyr, which is now Dragonspine in Mondstadt. Refugees from a land of snow and strife settled the then-green mountain, and their kingdom prospered under the heavens' blessing. Then the Skyfrost Nail fell from the sky. Endless blizzards buried the kingdom, its sacred white tree was shattered, and its people died. Today only frozen ruins remain, along with murals, carved tablets and a few personal keepsakes.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Sal Vindagnyr is a dead kingdom whose ruins lie frozen under Dragonspine's snow. The Skyfrost Nail that destroyed it hovers, restored, above the summit.

59.content:
Schulz's Blacksmith (also: Schulz Smithshop): Schulz's Blacksmith is the main forge in Mondstadt City, near the front gate. Wagner the blacksmith and his apprentice Schulz run it, and it forges and sells weapons.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1, as far as sources show.

60.content:
Shattuck: Shattuck is a restaurant in the village of Millhaven in northern Mondstadt. Benthem owns it. It sells simple food and cooking ingredients and first appeared in Version 6.5.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1, as far as sources show.

61.content:
Skyfrost Nail (also: Nail of Cold Heavens): The Skyfrost Nail is the Celestial Nail (a "Nail of Retribution") planted at the summit of Dragonspine in Mondstadt, and the summit area takes its name from it. It looks like a colossal broken crystalline pillar. Thousands of years ago it fell from the heavens onto the green mountain of Vindagnyr, burying the kingdom of Sal Vindagnyr under the endless snow that still makes Dragonspine deadly. In the Traveler's time its scattered shards were rejoined, and it now hovers in the air above the peak.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Skyfrost Nail is whole again and hovers above Dragonspine's summit. After the Ruler of Death Ronova's last act in Snezhnaya, it is giving off the same strange mark of light into the sky as the other Nails of Retribution across Teyvat, and Albedo is studying it.

62.content: Snow-Covered Path: The Snow-Covered Path is the trail up the lower slopes of Dragonspine, Mondstadt's permanently frozen mountain. It is coated in ice all the way up, and the Dragonspine Adventurer Camp and the Frostbearing Tree lie along it.

63.content:
Spiral Abyss (also: Abyssus Obscura, Abyss Corridor, Abyssal Moon Spire, Moment of Syzygy): The Spiral Abyss is a special domain on Musk Reef, an island off Cape Oath in Galesong Hill. In-game text calls it a massive underground city built by an ancient civilization long gone, whose purpose remains unknown, with forgotten secrets and treasures buried within. Its first-entry message calls it an inverse tower, and gives it the Latin name Abyssus Obscura, "Dark Abyss". Monsters and humans alike flock to it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Spiral Abyss remains open as a permanent special domain.

64.content:
Springvale (also: Springvale village, Clear Spring Town): Springvale is a small, peaceful hunting village in Windwail Highland, south of Mondstadt City and facing the lake around it. It is a cluster of one-storey tan houses with blue-tiled roofs, a single windmill, and a natural spring beneath it. Most residents are hunters who supply fresh meat to Mondstadt's restaurants, and the village attracts tourists with its rustic charm. Locals pass down a legend of a benevolent spirit living in the spring.

Status as of 7.1: Quiet and unchanged as of 7.1.

65.content:
Starfell Lake (also: The Marsh of Celestial Guardians): Starfell Lake is a lake and marsh in Starfell Valley, Mondstadt, near Mondstadt City and the Whispering Woods. A Statue of The Seven stands here. In the Prologue it is where the Traveler first felt Anemo power answer and glimpsed a green dragon flying toward a distant forest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is an ordinary, calm area of Mondstadt; no later story has changed it.

66.content:
Starfell Valley: Starfell Valley is the central and most varied region of Mondstadt, running from Stormbearer Point on the south coast to the Whispering Woods. Its centre is Cider Lake, on whose island stands Mondstadt City, and it is where the Knights of Favonius mainly carry out their duty of protecting locals and travelers. Lakes, woods, ruins and cliffs make it the area most visitors, including the Traveler at the start of the story, first see.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Starfell Valley is the calm, patrolled centre of Mondstadt; the pages read for this entry record no new threat here after 1.0.

67.content: Starglow Cavern: Starglow Cavern is a great, icy cave in the depths of Dragonspine. Strange blue plants called Starglow light even its darkest passages, and before the quest In the Mountains it held one of the three shards of the Skyfrost Nail.

68.content:
Starsnatch Cliff (also: Star-Plucking Cliff): Starsnatch Cliff is a scenic cliff in Starfell Valley, Mondstadt, with a wide view of the night sky. At night the secret couple Marla and Marvin meet here. The Midsummer Courtyard domain, an ancient ruin, lies beside it. In the Prologue it is where Venti, Jean, Diluc and the Traveler gathered before purifying the dragon Stormterror.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the cliff is unchanged: the lovers still meet here at night and the domain remains. No later story has altered it.

69.content: Stormbearer Mountains: The Stormbearer Mountains are the high country in the north of Starfell Valley, once a place to observe approaching storms. Now only an abandoned watchtower stands there, and monsters roam the slopes.

70.content: Stormbearer Point: Stormbearer Point is a headland in Starfell Valley. The coast just south of it is where the Traveler begins their journey across Teyvat with Paimon. A Church of Favonius nun named Vind keeps a storm watch here, and a Knight named Harry patrols near the waypoint.

71.content:
Stormterror's Lair (also: Old Mondstadt, Dvalin's Lair, Abandoned Capital of Howling Winds): Stormterror's Lair is the ruin of Old Mondstadt, the capital that the tyrannical God of Storms, Decarabian, built in the Brightcrown Mountains of northwestern Mondstadt. A ring-shaped city surrounds his broken central tower. The city has been empty since his fall about 2,600 years ago. Later the wounded dragon Dvalin came here to rest, and the people of Mondstadt, who had forgotten him and feared him, called him "Stormterror", which gave the ruins their name. In the Prologue, the Traveler, Venti, Jean and Diluc fought their way to the top of the tower to free Dvalin from the Abyss Order's corruption.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Stormterror's Lair is a deserted ruin and a known landmark north of Mondstadt City. Dvalin, now reconciled with Mondstadt, comes and goes, and is often absent.

72.content: Symbol of Mondstadt's Hero (also: Mondstadt's Hero Oak, Vennessa's oak): The Symbol of Mondstadt's Hero is the enormous oak tree at Windrise in Galesong Hill. Mondstadt believes it grew after the hero Vennessa ascended to Celestia about a thousand years ago. A Statue of the Seven stands under its branches.

73.content:
Taste of the North: Taste of the North is a restaurant in Dornman Port, owned by Frith, who is said to come from Nod-Krai. It sells simple Mondstadt food and cooking ingredients, and first appeared in Version 6.5. The name is the wiki's unofficial label.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1, as far as sources show.

key: Temple of the Falcon of the West
Deep Within the Temple of the Falcon
74.content:
Temple of the Falcon (also: Falcon Temple, Temple of the Falcon of the West, Deep Within the Temple of the Falcon, Abyssal Traces): The Temple of the Falcon is a ruined temple at Windrise in Galesong Hill, between Mondstadt City and the great oak where Vennessa is said to have ascended. It was devoted to the Falcon of the West, one of the Four Winds, and has been abandoned for centuries. Its in-game description says it has watched over Windrise for thousands of years, and that perhaps the winds of the past still linger in its halls.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is an abandoned, little-visited ruin at Windrise, its story domains complete and its one-time domain enterable.

key: Temple of the Lion of the South
Deep Within the Temple of the Lion
75.content:
Temple of the Lion (also: Lion Temple, Temple of the Lion of the South, Deep Within the Temple of the Lion): The Temple of the Lion is a ruined temple on Falcon Coast in Galesong Hill, devoted to the Lion of the South, one of the Four Winds. It has long been abandoned, and its ruins show signs of monster activity. Folklore holds that the dandelions seen riding the winds across Mondstadt symbolise the Lion's blessing.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 an abandoned ruin on Falcon Coast; its story domain is complete and its one-time domain and Elemental Trials remain available.

key: Temple of the Wolf of the North
Deep Within the Temple of the Wolf
76.content:
Temple of the Wolf (also: Wolf Temple, Temple of the Wolf of the North, Deep Within the Temple of the Wolf): The Temple of the Wolf is a ruined temple of the Four Winds near the Thousand Winds Temple in Starfell Valley, devoted to the Wolf of the North. The priests are gone and monsters have seized it, though the spirit of the Wolf is said still to watch over Mondstadt's fields from elsewhere. Its depths are described as a destroyed ancient training ground.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is an abandoned ruin; its story domain is complete and its one-time domain remains enterable.

77.content:
The Cat's Tail (also: Cat's Tail, Cats Tail): The Cat's Tail is a tavern in Mondstadt City, owned by Margaret and known for its cats and for Diona, its young bartender whose cocktails taste wonderful whatever goes into them. It sits between the Adventurers' Guild post and the Good Hunter restaurant, and is where Mondstadt's Genius Invokation TCG players meet.

People: Margaret owns the tavern. Diona is its star bartender. Prince, a black cat, is the tavern's TCG helper.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the tavern is open and the TCG hub of Mondstadt; no later content changes that.

key: Thorny Crown of the Mountain Wind
78.comment: Thorny Crown of the Mountain Wind
78.content:
Thorny Crown of the Mountain Wind: Thorny Crown of the Mountain Wind is a Domain of Blessing in Windrest Peak, northern Mondstadt, added in version 6.6. Its description calls it a floral realm hidden amid the mountains, seldom visited because it is remote. Its lore blurb recalls Elysium, an ancient city-state whose people believed it, sealed in its coffin, would outlast corruption and flourish like a sacred forest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the domain is open; it was added in 6.6 and no later content changes it.

79.content:
Thousand Winds Temple (also: Ancient Thousand Winds Temple): The Thousand Winds Temple is a ruined temple and amphitheater in Starfell Valley. The Arcadians built it to worship Istaroth, Ruler of Time; later it served both Istaroth and Barbatos, and in the aristocratic age it became an arena where slaves fought for the nobles' amusement. It is also where the future Anemo Archon, then a small wind spirit, was first answered.

Status as of 7.1: A ruin as of 7.1, still visited by researchers.

80.content:
Valley of Remembrance (also: Dance of Steel): The Valley of Remembrance is a Domain of Blessing between Dawn Winery and Dragonspine in Mondstadt. Its entrance text says that after a time the continent's people lost track of the past and dug downward to find what they had forgotten; beyond an ancient tree's hollow, yesterday's secrets became today's treasures. It is an altar full of monsters that fear brute force, and clearing it rewards artifacts.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the domain is open and unchanged since 1.0.

81.content:
Whispering Woods (also: Whispering Forest): The Whispering Woods are dense, deep woods in Starfell Valley, near Starfell Lake and Mondstadt City, cut by a small road. Wind in the leaves sounds like whispers, hence the name. In the Prologue the Traveler first sees Venti, then just a boy, calming the dragon Dvalin here.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the woods are unchanged; no later story has used them.

82.content:
Windrest Peak: Windrest Peak is the northernmost part of Mondstadt, opened in Version 6.5, and revolves around the port town of Dornman Port, one of the continent's major trade hubs. It also holds Millhaven, an idyllic windmill village of windrest-flower fields and fragrance makers, and the Old Sanatorium Site, where a hilltop sanatorium once stood. High above the peak floats the Temple of Space. The weather is clearer and more varied than in the rest of Mondstadt.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Windrest Peak is open, busy and calm; no 7.0-7.1 event is recorded in the pages read.

83.content:
Windrise: Windrise is a plain of everlasting breeze in Galesong Hill, in Mondstadt's countryside near the sea. A giant oak, the Symbol of Mondstadt's Hero, dominates it. According to legend the tree grew where the hero Vennessa, first Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, ascended to Celestia about a thousand years ago. A Statue of the Seven stands beneath its branches, and locals treat the place with quiet reverence.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Windrise is unchanged: a peaceful landmark and memorial.

84.content:
Windwail Highland: Windwail Highland is the rustic southwestern part of Mondstadt, a country of clear springs, orchards and lush forest. It holds Springvale, a sleepy hunting village built over a spring; the Dawn Winery, the chief winery of Mondstadt, owned by the Ragnvindr family and now by Diluc; and Wolvendom, a dark forest ruled by the wolf-god Boreas and his pack, which the locals avoid.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Windwail Highland is quiet. Diluc runs the winery and Boreas still holds Wolvendom; none of the pages read records a change to the area in 7.0-7.1 content.

85.content:
With Wind Comes Glory: With Wind Comes Glory is a popular souvenir shop in Mondstadt City, run by Marjorie. Adventurers can pawn precious items there for Anemo Sigils and spend the Sigils on rare goods.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1, as far as sources show.

86.content:
Wolvendom: Wolvendom is a deep, dark forest in Windwail Highland, Mondstadt, so silent that it chills the spine. It is the domain of Boreas, also called Andrius, the Wolf of the North of the Four Winds, and his wolf pack. Locals avoid it, and not even fearless hunters enter lightly. The boy Razor, raised by the wolves, lives here.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the pack and Boreas' spirit still hold Wolvendom; Razor lives there.

87.content:
Wyrmrest Valley: Wyrmrest Valley is a steep valley on Dragonspine, Mondstadt, where the black dragon Durin fell about 500 years ago. His skull, ribcage and heart lie there, and the life force seeping from his core has dyed the silver snow scarlet. It is cold, dangerous and eerie, and the Fatui have been interested in it.

Status as of 7.1: Durin's core is drained and inert as of 7.1; the dragon is replaced by the human Durin.
